clue.text: A bit of flower power? Duck out

indicators.note: the duck sits out, on the outside, with the other piece placed within it

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A wry aside about flower power, followed by a shout to someone to dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower power' looks like a single phrase from the sixties, but 'power' is split off to give P, which goes inside TEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepal is one segment of a flower's perianth where petals and sepals look alike, so it is literally a part of the bloom.

clue.text: Scent enveloping a couple of females in bar at rear of ship

indicators.note: the scent wraps around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a trail is the scent left by an animal
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A whiff of perfume surrounds two women in a pub, set at the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub for the females, but it is the rail of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the handrail around a ship's stern, a bar at the rear.

clue.text: Chemist quick to bandage injury

indicators.note: the word for quick wraps around the injury as a bandage would

parts.note: pacy means fast or quick
harm is injury or damage

explanation.surface: A pharmacist is hurrying to dress a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a chemist's shop, and 'chemist' is the British name for it.

clue.text: Ignore new hotel, built with minimum of taste, degrading all around?

indicators.note: the letters are built up into something new, rearranged
the least possible amount of the word, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to overlook a new hotel thrown up with little taste that cheapens the whole neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: IGNORE, NEW and HOTEL plus T, the first letter of 'taste', are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering the tone means making a place or conversation more vulgar, degrading it for everyone present.

clue.text: Keeping careful watch on bomb, I take brief look around

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another follows it, so the bomb's letter comes first

parts.note: the V1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War, written here with the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the brief look goes around the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a glance is a quick, brief look

explanation.surface: Someone stays alert beside a bomb, glancing round it now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The bomb is the German V1 of the Second World War, its 1 written as a Roman I; 'on' places the rest after it in this across clue, and 'take' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilance is the state of keeping a careful watch for danger, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Part of survival test

indicators.note: only a portion of the following word is used, its letters lying within

explanation.surface: A section of a survival exercise is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral examination, especially for a university degree, so it is a test.

clue.text: Re-steaming cooked sprouts

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Brussels sprouts are being steamed again in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprouts' looks like the vegetable, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is to begin growing, so it means sprouts as a verb.

clue.text: Shoot weak ruler: unusual approach to solving the problem

definitions.text: unusual approach to solving the problem

parts.note: a lateral is a side shoot growing from a plant's main stem
thin can mean weak, as in a thin excuse
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A drastic solution: just shoot the feeble monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking means solving problems by an indirect, creative approach rather than conventional logic.

clue.text: Ambassador, one in care of sister at first

indicators.note: the sister is placed at the start of the answer

parts.note: a sister is a nun

indicators.note: one goes inside the care-of abbreviation

parts.note: c/o is the abbreviation for care of, on letters
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An envoy, one person in the care of a nun at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal ambassador, the Pope's diplomatic representative to a state.

clue.text: City's without name, omitted from register

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: the name's letter is left out of the word for register

parts.note: to enter is to register, record in a list

explanation.surface: A city goes unnamed, left off an official list.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the county city of Devon in south-west England, a cathedral city.

clue.text: Patriot seen to tire and falter

parts.note: to flag is to tire or lose energy
to waver is to falter or hesitate

explanation.surface: A patriot is spotted growing weary and losing resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag-waver is someone who displays patriotism showily, so the phrase names an enthusiastic patriot.

clue.text: Unable to relax, needing pain-relief technique applied to end of toe

parts.note: TENS is transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation, a pain-relief method using mild currents

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is the one taken

explanation.surface: Someone too wound up to relax is being treated with electrical pain relief on a toe.
explanation.walkthrough: TENS is a known medical abbreviation: a small device that passes gentle electric pulses through the skin to ease pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense means being taut and stressed, the opposite of relaxed.

clue.text: Comment on book

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
Mark is a book of the New Testament, one of the Gospels

explanation.surface: Someone passes judgement on a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken or written comment, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fighter aircraft came down after losing tail, causing suffering?

parts.note: a MiG is a Soviet or Russian fighter jet, named after its designers Mikoyan and Gurevich

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, its tail

parts.note: rain came down: it rained

explanation.surface: A fighter jet comes down after losing its tail section, bringing pain to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring headache, a form of suffering; the question mark admits the definition is by example.

clue.text: Dour rector moving in direction of Old Bailey?

indicators.note: the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim clergyman is heading towards the Old Bailey, London's criminal court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bailey is the Central Criminal Court in London. The definition is cryptic: a court order is a direction from a court such as it.
explanation.definitionFit: A court order is a direction issued by a court, and the Old Bailey is a court.

clue.text: In cabinet, Labour's kept moaning endlessly?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Labour is kept within the cabinet, held inside it

parts.note: a console is a cabinet, for instance one housing a radio or television
Lab is the abbreviation for the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A political sketch of a Labour cabinet whose members never stop complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests government ministers, but here it is a piece of furniture, a cabinet for a radio or television.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inconsolable cannot be comforted, so they might well keep moaning without end; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Type of explosive used in missiles before dark, say

indicators.note: the missiles come before the next piece

parts.note: ammo, ammunition, is bullets and shells, things fired as missiles

indicators.note: say signals the next piece as it is pronounced, in its informal phonetic form

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: An explosive packed in missiles before nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonite is a type of explosive based on ammonium nitrate, used in mining.

clue.text: Rose, when epic finally reached conclusion

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: ended means came to a close

explanation.surface: A film named Rose, with the epic finally finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascended means went up, as does rose, the past tense of rise.

clue.text: Affordable housing not hard to find in Horsham street development

indicators.note: the letters of the place and street are developed into something new

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Cheap homes, minus the hard sell, are going up in a new Horsham street.
explanation.walkthrough: HORSHAM STREET without H ('not hard') rearranges into the answer. Horsham is a market town in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Starter homes are small, low-cost houses built for first-time buyers, i.e. affordable housing.

clue.text: Bolshie-sounding apprentice

indicators.note: the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Bolshie is short for Bolshevik, and a commie is a communist

explanation.surface: A trainee with a rebellious streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolshie' in British English usually means stroppy, but here it is the political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A commis is a junior chef or waiter, an apprentice in a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Drunk makes fuss, getting a round

parts.note: to make a stink is to make a fuss
O is a round shape, a circle

explanation.surface: A drunk causes a fuss when buying a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinko is slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Credit once so arranged without discussion

definitions.meaning: an old slang sense of the phrase was buying on credit, on tick
a proposal passed by a mere nod of assent, with no debate

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase once meant on credit and still means agreed by assent without debate.

clue.text: Wage leaving immigrant a bit short

indicators.note: the word is cut short by a bit, losing its last letter

parts.note: an incomer is a newcomer to a place, an immigrant

explanation.surface: Someone's pay does not stretch far once a newcomer leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is the money one earns, so a wage is a form of it.

clue.text: Working with engineers in former times

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
CE stands for Civil Engineers or civil engineering

explanation.surface: Things were done with engineers in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, in former times.

clue.text: Fruit gives chap an attack of illness

parts.note: a chap is a man
a go is a bout or attack, as in a nasty go of flu

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit gives a man a stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit, an example of the class.

clue.text: Flamboyantly dressed martial artist challenged out loud

indicators.note: the words are to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: a dan is a graded expert in judo or karate; to defy is to challenge, so defied means challenged

explanation.surface: A showily dressed martial artist issues a loud challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandified describes someone dressed like a dandy, showily and with great care for fashion.

clue.text: Shrub to me reeks foul

indicators.note: foul suggests something fouled up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a bush smells awful to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The smoke tree is a shrub whose feathery flower heads look like puffs of smoke.

clue.text: Vice ring ultimately exposed by film director

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: Sir Carol Reed was a British film director, of The Third Man

explanation.surface: A vice ring is uncovered by a film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is a vice.
